summary: Introductory Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and fidelity/latency tradeoffs. Customer is CedarBridge Health; they care about sub-200ms median, 99th <400ms for short clinical prompts, plus SOC2 and data residency. Agreed pilot steps and deliverables.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (SE), Rosa (SE), Alex, Priya, Tom, Marisa (CedarBridge)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec. quick round robin — if you can say role and the one thing you want from this session.
[00:12] Alex: Alex, ML platform, main ask is a clear path to get INT8 without clinical hallucinations — we care about accuracy for short discharge-summary prompts.
[00:22] Priya: Priya SRE — we need latency SLOs, 99th percentile guarantees and how that degrades under load.
[00:30] Tom: Tom — Head of AI — overall want recommendations: when to use FP8 vs INT8, and how to measure perceived quality.
[00:39] Maya: Great; we'll demo Optimize console for qprofiles, show a couple of perf runs from our sandbox, and map next steps for a 2-week pilot.

[02:05] Liam: Quick note, some of the product names might come out weird from transcription — but the core is qprofiles: these are per-route quantization settings that pick kernels and fallback.
[02:18] Rosa: we'll show an example where INT8 gets you 2.3x throughput improvement on A100-ish hosts for short contexts but there's a sensitivity hit on numeric fidelity, especially in clinical tokens.

[04:01] Alex: When you say sensitivity, is that deterministic or prompt-dependent?
[04:08] Rosa: mostly prompt-dependent — we run a sensitivity sweep with representative prompt sets, and Optimize surfaces a fidelity delta heatmap. the console shows per-prompt degradation and helps pick a hybrid profile.

[06:10] Maya: we'll share the sandbox spreadsheet later but quick numbers: for 64-token responses median latency on FP16 baseline was ~120ms, INT8 tuned got median to ~52ms, FP8 sat around ~70ms with better fidelity. 99th tails: FP16 ~360ms, INT8 worst-case ~520ms unless we enable smart fallback.
[06:45] Priya: those 99th numbers are a bit high for us, we target 99th <400ms. how does fallback affect tail latency?
[06:56] Liam: fallback adds a small followup penalty — the first call returns quickly from INT8 but if the eval detects quality regression the runtime issues a re-run on FP8/FP16. the user-visible latency is then the cold path (so worst-case rises). we typically recommend async verification for non-blocking ux or headroom on p99 when you want strict SLA.

[09:00] Tom: Can you do partial responses/streaming to hide re-run cost?
[09:06] Rosa: yes streaming + prefix caching helps. if the initial INT8 emits a short low-risk prefix we stream that, while the full-fidelity run completes and replaces content for sensitive fields. it's a UX trade.

[10:28] Alex: How do you quantify "perceived" quality vs token-level metrics? we care about hallucination rate not just token perplexity.
[10:37] Liam: we use a combination: rouge/bleu-style overlap for structured outputs, and human-labeled safety checks for hallucinations. Optimize ties evals to prompt sets and surfaces a degradation score and a per-example diff. for the pilot we recommend a small human-in-the-loop eval set focusing on hallucinations.

[13:12] Priya: Security — we need SOC2, SSO + SAML and customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. can you confirm those are available in the private/dedicated options?
[13:24] Maya: yes — Dedicated and Private support SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations, and audit logs. we'll attach the SOC2 appendix; Private also offers VPC peering and on-prem packaging.

[15:50] Alex: On the topic of cached KV — would the prefix cache cause data leakage between tenants?
[15:58] Liam: no — caches are isolated per-customer and per-model-version; for Dedicated we can pin to hardware pools and disable cross-tenant caching. we also have TTL controls and scrub policies.

[18:05] Tom: What's the expected cost delta? INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16 unit cost?
[18:12] Rosa: ballpark, INT8 can be 35-55% cheaper per-token, FP8 ~20-35% cheaper, depending on batch and seq length. the console cost model projects per-route cost given token distribution you upload.

[21:30] Maya: let's walk the console — (screen share audible) here's the qprofile editor: you can target routes by tag, pick base precision, enable smart fallback, and set quality thresholds.
[22:05] Liam: note the "sensitivity sweep" — it runs a set of prompt permutations across precisions and outputs a ranked list of candidates with expected latency/cost and a fidelity drop metric.

[25:40] Alex: can we enforce "never degrade critical fields"? for e.g. diagnosis codes must be exact.
[25:47] Rosa: yes you can mark structured fields and the eval will treat them as hard constraints — then Optimize will only pick profiles that preserve exact-match on those fields or flag them for fallback.

[28:10] Priya: operationally, how does autoscaling interact with quantized models? if we get a burst what happens to the p99?
[28:20] Liam: autoscaler spins up more instances; warmup for large KV caches can affect p99. Optimize recommends pre-warming policies for predicted bursts, and we support burst capacity in Dedicated where you pay an overtime buffer to keep tail low.

[31:00] Tom: Are there known failure modes with INT8 at long contexts?
[31:07] Rosa: long-contexts can amplify quantization noise in attention, we often see degradation after 1k tokens on certain architectures. for long-form clinical notes we either use FP8 or hybrid profiles that switch precision after window boundaries.

[33:58] Alex: For the pilot, we'd like a smoke test: 1) run 3 prompt sets (short clinical, mid-length summarization, long-context note) 2) check hallucination delta and p99 latency 3) recommend profile and rollout plan. is that feasible in two weeks?
[34:15] Maya: yes that's exactly our standard pilot. we'll provision a sandbox, run the sensitivity sweep, then cut a canary route for 1-2% traffic in your staging and measure.

[36:40] Priya: timeline questions — provisioning, peering, and compliance review — how long before we can start?
[36:48] Liam: peering typically 3-5 business days, sandbox can be live in 48 hours with default configs. compliance packets we can share today.

[39:22] Tom: competitor question — if we already have some infra with Vertex endpoints, why Redwood?
[39:30] Maya: key differentiators: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, explicit Optimize tooling for qprofiles, cost-driven suggestions and rollback policies. we focus on serving economics and predictable SLAs rather than just model access.

[41:55] Rosa: Also we'll demo the telemetry hooks — token-level latency, token-level cost, and per-prompt fidelity diffs so you can attribute regression to prompts, not models.

[45:12] Alex: small nit — can we get the perf numbers on our hardware targets (NVIDIA H100 vs A100)?
[45:20] Liam: yes we'll include both in the perf spreadsheet; H100 tends to narrow the INT8 vs FP8 gap. we'll surface device-specific kernel choices in the report.

[47:40] Maya: ok recap: deliverables: perf spreadsheet (device-specific), sandbox runbook, qprofile seeds, security appendix. action items on owners as noted.

[49:10] Marisa: quick privacy question — will logs from the pilot include PHI in plain text? we need guidance on masking.
[49:18] Maya: by default telemetry includes token metadata but we can scrub and encrypt logs, and we can skip storing request text for the pilot. we'll document masking options in the security appendix.

[52:00] Alex: final — show of hands for go-ahead to schedule pilot kickoff next week. (several yes)
[52:13] Maya: great, I'll follow up with calendar invite and attach the perf template. thanks everyone.

[54:30] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (qprofile -> q-profile, KV cache spelled as K-V cache), speaker overlaps, some filler words removed for readability.
